correctness.rationale: Three unique Lagrange weights follow by integrating degree-two cardinal polynomials; exact sign inequalities in centered coordinates imply at most one negative weight. Direct two-variable integration gives each event probability. In spacing coordinates, the double-small-gap region gives the sharp coefficient 12 times integral_0^1(x²−x+1/3)dx=2 through an exact hyperbolic area identity. The complement where one gap is at least fixed delta has O_delta(1/t) tail. Squeezing then letting delta→0 establishes the limit, while layer cake establishes precisely q<1 for finite positive moments. The included standalone exact-fraction and quadrature checks reproduce finite identities only; the analytic proof carries the infinite assertion.

value.rationale: The total absolute quadrature weight is exactly the amplification norm for bounded sampled-value errors. With only three random candidates, fixed-degree interpolatory quadrature is a natural minimal test of positive-weight design. Exact positive-weight success probability and a log-enhanced L1 heavy tail distinguish random unmodified points from positive-weight selection and separated-node schemes. The leading constant and four sign events are useful benchmarks; the claim does not purport to prove uniform accuracy for arbitrary integrands or offer a higher-dimensional theorem.
